policy_direction_of_yea: Expand mandatory collection of a local solicitor fee to all criminal matters in which court costs are assessed and bar waiving that fee unless every other court charge is waived.
position_summary: Sponsored a Pickens County bill expanding criminal-case fee collection and restricting selective judicial waiver of the solicitor fee.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. This is a local court-finance measure with a marginally conservative punitive/fee-collection direction; it is not evidence of a broad statewide criminal-justice platform. The progressive model label is unsupported.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize Tuscaloosa red-light cameras and owner-based civil enforcement while capping fines and adding notice, appeal, record, insurance, and anti-incarceration safeguards.
position_summary: Co-sponsored Tuscaloosa's red-light-camera authorization, expanding automated civil enforcement but pairing it with substantial due-process and collateral-consequence protections.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The principal direction expands surveillance and civil enforcement; safeguards make the ideological valence mixed. Treat as a local traffic-enforcement position, not a broad criminal-justice ideology indicator.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit public law-enforcement agencies from charging insurers, motorists, or vehicle owners a separate fee for responding to or investigating a motor-vehicle accident.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a statewide ban on accident-response service fees, limiting government fee collection and shielding motorists and insurers from an added charge.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The queue's criminal-justice label is too broad; this is primarily a government-fee and consumer-cost measure. Its anti-fee direction can read as fiscally conservative while its cost protection is not cleanly ideological.

policy_direction_of_yea: Bar new permitted landfills and junkyards outside municipal limits within one mile of the Chattahoochee River, except facilities located on an industrial site.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a regulatory buffer preventing new landfills and junkyards near the Chattahoochee River.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The measure is geographically narrow but directly supports preventive waterway protection through land-use regulation. The Ministral conservative label is unsupported by the enacted policy direction.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend the Coosa Valley Resource Conservation and Development Council for receiving a federal partnership award.
position_summary: Joined a chamber-wide ceremonial commendation of a regional conservation organization.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. This is a nearly chamber-wide ceremonial recognition with no policy, appropriation, regulation, or reliable evidence of an individual environmental position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create an interagency commission to coordinate transportation access for people with disabilities, older adults, and low-income residents while reducing duplicative rules and identifying cost-effective service strategies.
position_summary: Co-sponsored creation of a statewide interagency body focused on improving coordinated transportation access for disabled, elderly, and low-income Alabamians.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The bill creates planning and coordination duties rather than a direct appropriation, but it is substantive evidence of prioritizing access to human-service transportation for vulnerable populations.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require a three-fifths vote in each legislative chamber before a state mental-health institution may be leased, transferred, or placed under nongovernmental management.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a high legislative barrier to privatizing or outsourcing management of state mental-health institutions.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is directly anti-privatization and pro-legislative oversight of public institutions. Both model labels of conservative conflate greater legislative control with conservative policy; relative to a free-market/privatization dimension, the direction is progressive, though it does not prove a position on mental-health funding levels.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Tuscaloosa-area local governments to study purchasing the privately owned Black Warrior River toll bridge, retaining tolls until the purchase price is repaid and then ending them.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a feasibility study of local public acquisition of a privately owned toll bridge, with the stated goal of ultimately eliminating the toll.
review_note: Full resolution text and both model reviews examined. The resolution is nonbinding and geographically narrow, so it supports only a modest local position: openness to public ownership of infrastructure where sponsors argued it could improve access and economic development.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend Huntsville's effort to become a Google Fiber test market.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of Huntsville's Google Fiber application.
review_note: Full resolution and both model reviews examined. This is symbolic recognition without an appropriation, regulatory change, or governmental commitment; it is not reliable evidence of an individual broadband or economic-policy position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend Fayette County members of the University of Alabama Crimsonettes.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of local students serving in the University of Alabama Crimsonettes.
review_note: Full resolution and both model reviews examined. This is a local ceremonial honor and supplies no substantive education-policy evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend Huntsville's effort to become a Google Fiber test market.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of Huntsville's Google Fiber application.
review_note: Full resolution and both model reviews examined. This House resolution duplicates the policy-free commendation reflected in HJR558; it is not reliable evidence of an individual broadband or economic-policy position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend Fayette County members of the University of Alabama Crimsonettes.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of local students serving in the University of Alabama Crimsonettes.
review_note: Full resolution and both model reviews examined. This joint resolution duplicates the local ceremonial honor in HR352 and supplies no substantive education-policy evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow a teacher or school official to satisfy the child-abuse reporting mandate by giving a written report to a principal or superintendent by the close of the next school day, with that administrator then responsible for forwarding it to authorities.
position_summary: Co-sponsored replacing educators' immediate direct-report obligation with an internal written-report safe harbor and an administrator forwarding duty.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The bill formalizes responsibility and documentation inside schools, but it also delays and redirects the existing immediate direct-report rule. Those competing child-protection and institutional-liability effects make the ideological direction mixed; neither model's one-direction label is adequately supported.

policy_direction_of_yea: Extend the Lieutenant Governor's Commission on Public-Private Partnership Projects through the fifth legislative day of the 2011 session and direct it to continue implementing recommendations from its earlier report.
position_summary: Co-sponsored extending the state's public-private infrastructure commission and continuing work on its prior recommendations.
review_note: Full enrolled resolution reviewed. This is more than a commendation: it sustains a government body and endorses continued implementation work. But the incorporated recommendations are not stated in this text, so it evidences a public-private-infrastructure priority without supporting a clean progressive or conservative direction.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Congress to provide $3 million for renovating the Alabama Farmers Market, including modernized agricultural facilities, neighborhood revitalization, and job creation in a low-income area.
position_summary: Co-sponsored seeking federal investment to renovate the Alabama Farmers Market and support agricultural commerce, neighborhood revitalization, and local jobs.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. The heading contains an apparent drafting error ('$38 million'), but every operative and explanatory reference requests $3 million. Sponsorship is direct evidence of support for targeted public investment in agricultural and neighborhood economic development.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Congress to provide $3 million for renovating the Alabama Farmers Market, including modernized agricultural facilities, neighborhood revitalization, and job creation in a low-income area.
position_summary: Co-sponsored seeking federal investment to renovate the Alabama Farmers Market and support agricultural commerce, neighborhood revitalization, and local jobs.
review_note: Full joint-resolution text and both model reviews examined. This is the companion version of HR439 and supports the same targeted public-investment position. The heading's '$38 million' conflicts with the consistent $3 million request in the operative text, which controls this summary.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a voluntary state-income-tax refund checkoff to supplement education benefits for disabled Alabama veterans, with administrative costs capped at 10 percent.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a voluntary refund-donation mechanism dedicated to supplemental education benefits for disabled veterans.
review_note: Full engrossed text reviewed. The voluntary funding mechanism is compatible with limited-government preferences, but the enacted policy expands a state-administered benefit for disabled veterans; code as modestly progressive on social services rather than as evidence of a broad tax position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Exempt Eagles' Wings, Inc., a Tuscaloosa-area nonprofit serving adults with developmental disabilities, from state, county, and municipal sales and use taxes.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a targeted tax exemption for a nonprofit provider of day and residential services to adults with developmental disabilities.
review_note: Full enrolled bill reviewed and organizational identity verified through the Alabama Department of Mental Health provider directory and the nonprofit's mission statement. This is narrow evidence of using tax policy to support disability services, not a general tax-cut position; confidence is medium because the bill text itself names but does not describe the beneficiary.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require a public forum and unanimous joint county-municipal approval before a municipality licenses a junkyard in its extraterritorial police jurisdiction, then assign post-license enforcement to the county.
position_summary: Co-sponsored stronger public-participation and intergovernmental approval requirements for junkyards outside municipal limits.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The bill raises the procedural barrier to siting a junkyard and adds a public forum, which is modestly regulatory/progressive on environmental land use. Its assignment of enforcement to counties is an administrative feature, not a basis for the conservative model label.

policy_direction_of_yea: Impose a three-year moratorium on new death sentences and executions while Alabama adopts specified safeguards for competent defense, post-conviction review, racial fairness, and protection of juveniles and people with intellectual disabilities.
position_summary: Co-sponsored pausing Alabama's death penalty for three years to implement fairness and due-process reforms in capital cases.
review_note: Full bill text and both concordant model reviews examined. This is direct, strongly directional evidence of a death-penalty reform position. The model claim that every sponsor was Republican is unsupported metadata commentary and was disregarded; the policy classification rests on the official text.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require first-time used-vehicle dealers and wholesalers to complete at least four hours of state-approved legal-compliance training before licensure, while exempting existing licensees in good standing.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a new training prerequisite for first-time used-vehicle dealer and wholesaler licenses as a consumer-protection measure.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The measure adds a modest entry requirement and state approval of seminar providers, making it regulatory/progressive on occupational licensing even though its stated purpose is public protection and it grandfathers current licensees.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a diverse interagency commission with facility access and beneficiary input to recommend gender-responsive services, community alternatives, population reduction, reentry support, and racial and gender equity for girls and women in the justice system.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a commission charged with reducing gaps and inequities affecting incarcerated women and girls and expanding evidence-based alternatives and reentry services.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. This is substantive and strongly reform-oriented: it expressly targets gender equity, community-based services, alternatives to high-security confinement, reduced women's prison populations, and the well-being of incarcerated women and girls.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Alabama's governor and attorney general not to join litigation blocking implementation of the federal comprehensive health-care reform law, emphasizing affordable access and defending the law's constitutionality.
position_summary: Co-sponsored defending implementation of the Affordable Care Act against state litigation.
review_note: Full House resolution reviewed. Although nonbinding, it states an explicit and strongly directional health-policy position in the sponsors' own language; it is reliable public-position evidence rather than a ceremonial resolution.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Alabama's governor and attorney general not to join litigation blocking implementation of the federal comprehensive health-care reform law, emphasizing affordable access and defending the law's constitutionality.
position_summary: Co-sponsored defending implementation of the Affordable Care Act against state litigation.
review_note: Full joint resolution reviewed. This companion to HR763 states the same explicit and strongly directional health-policy position and is retained despite being nonbinding.

policy_direction_of_yea: Enact Alabama's fiscal-year 2011 Education Trust Fund budget for the support, maintenance, development, debt service, and capital needs of public education and related educational programs.
position_summary: Co-sponsored the fiscal-year 2011 public-education budget.
review_note: Full enrolled budget structure reviewed. Sponsorship is strong evidence that public education budgeting was a priority, but the omnibus allocation cannot be coded as uniformly expansionary without a prior-year counterfactual; retain as mixed rather than treating every line item as an individual position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Appropriate $9,703,990 from the Education Trust Fund to Tuskegee University, including at least $1,414,586 for agricultural research and extension, subject to planning, audit, and performance-reporting requirements.
position_summary: Co-sponsored state education funding for Tuskegee University and its agricultural research and extension work.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. This is direct evidence of support for public investment in a historically Black, state-related university, paired with fiscal-accountability requirements.

policy_direction_of_yea: Shift part of public-school bond debt service to the Education Trust Fund, reappropriate prior-year balances, cap the Department of Human Resources food-stamp-fund reversion, and dedicate excess funds to subsidized child-care slots.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an education-finance adjustment that also protected excess human-services funds for subsidized child care.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The bond-source change and reappropriations are fiscally technical, while the child-care dedication is substantively progressive; code the bundled bill as mixed and summarize the directly observable social-services priority without inferring a broader fiscal ideology.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow the Teachers' Retirement System to amortize its accrued pension liability over as many as 30 years instead of 20 years.
position_summary: Co-sponsored lengthening the funding period for the teachers' pension system's accrued liability.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. Extending amortization reduces near-term employer contribution pressure but delays full funding and can increase long-run financing costs; it is conservative on current-budget burden and less protective of pension funding, without changing promised benefits directly.

policy_direction_of_yea: Enact the fiscal-year 2011 omnibus General Fund budget for ordinary agency operations, government functions, debt service, and capital outlay.
position_summary: Co-sponsored the fiscal-year 2011 General Fund operating budget.
review_note: The enrolled omnibus budget was reviewed at the structural level. Sponsorship establishes participation in the core appropriations process but does not isolate a coherent issue stance across hundreds of unrelated allocations; exclude it from directional position evidence and rely on narrower appropriation bills where available.

policy_direction_of_yea: Appropriate $435,600 from the General Fund to the Alabama Coalition Against Domestic Violence, conditioned on audited financials, an operating plan, and quarterly and annual performance reports.
position_summary: Co-sponsored state funding for domestic-violence services with audit and performance safeguards.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. This is direct evidence of support for publicly funded domestic-violence services, with accountability conditions that do not change the underlying progressive service-investment direction.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allocate more than $94 million in tobacco-settlement funds to child welfare, Medicaid, mental health, public health, rehabilitation, youth services, senior services, and related programs, with quarterly allotment and performance controls.
position_summary: Co-sponsored substantial tobacco-settlement investment in children, health, disability, youth, and senior-service programs.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. Although it is a multi-program appropriation, its recipients consistently reflect a health-and-human-services investment priority and include explicit planning, outcome, and audit requirements.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow vending machines in the Bullock County jail and dedicate their profits to a sheriff-controlled fund usable exclusively for law-enforcement purposes.
position_summary: Sponsored a local jail-vending revenue mechanism for the Bullock County Sheriff's Office.
review_note: Full enrolled local act reviewed. This is a narrow administrative revenue measure with no statewide criminal-justice policy change or dependable ideological direction; retain as activity but exclude from candidate-position evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Provide eligible Department of Corrections employees working inside correctional facilities with conditional annual 2.5 percent pay steps, up to a cumulative 10 percent, in years without General Fund proration.
position_summary: Co-sponsored recurring salary increases for state corrections employees who work inside secured facilities.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is direct support for improved compensation of higher-risk public employees, moderated by a no-proration fiscal condition.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow the Barbour County Commission to add five dollars to the concealed-pistol permit fee and dedicate the proceeds to sheriff's-vehicle purchase and maintenance.
position_summary: Sponsored a modest increase in Barbour County's concealed-pistol permit fee to fund law-enforcement vehicles.
review_note: Full enrolled local act reviewed. The measure marginally increases the cost of carrying a concealed pistol and is therefore modestly progressive on gun regulation, though it is local and principally a sheriff-finance measure rather than evidence of broad gun-control views.

policy_direction_of_yea: Submit to voters a ten-year transfer of $100 million annually from the Alabama Trust Fund for state and local road, bridge, rail, maintenance, and economic-development infrastructure, with geographic allocation rules.
position_summary: Sponsored a constitutional amendment committing substantial Trust Fund resources to a decade-long state and local transportation investment program.
review_note: Full proposed amendment reviewed. The policy is strongly pro-public infrastructure investment and local capital funding. Its use of Trust Fund assets creates a fiscal tradeoff, so the progressive label describes investment direction rather than overall budget prudence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Honor Don Sutton by naming a segment of Alabama Highway 10 after him.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial highway designation honoring baseball player Don Sutton.
review_note: Full enrolled resolution reviewed. The highway naming is honorary and provides no infrastructure or economic-development position evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Honor Representative Lesley Vance by naming a segment of Highway 431 South after him.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial highway designation honoring a legislative colleague.
review_note: Full enrolled resolution reviewed. This is an honorary designation, not evidence of a transportation-policy position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend Tuskegee University's basketball team for winning its conference championship.
position_summary: Joined a chamber-wide ceremonial commendation of Tuskegee University's basketball team.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. This is a nearly unanimous athletic commendation and supplies no substantive higher-education policy evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Eliminate Alabama's state sales tax on most food while phasing down the federal-income-tax deduction for higher-income filers and retaining the full deduction below stated income thresholds.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a progressive tax shift that removed the state grocery tax and offset revenue by limiting a deduction concentrated among higher-income taxpayers.
review_note: Full proposed constitutional amendment reviewed. This is unusually clear distributive tax-policy evidence: it reduces a regressive consumption tax and narrows an income-tax preference above $50,000 for single filers and $100,000 for joint filers.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow parents of a stillborn child after the twentieth week of gestation to request a Certificate of Birth Resulting in Stillbirth for the ordinary certificate fee.
position_summary: Co-sponsored optional state recognition documents for families experiencing stillbirth.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The measure is an administrative and bereavement-recognition policy and does not change abortion law, fetal personhood, inheritance, or the definition of live birth. Do not use it as abortion-position evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Submit to voters a five-year dedication of offshore oil-and-gas capital payments, after debt service, to equally apportioned congressional-district job creation and retention projects selected by the governor and Alabama Development Office.
position_summary: Sponsored using offshore energy capital receipts for geographically distributed job-creation and job-retention investments.
review_note: Full proposed constitutional amendment reviewed. This is targeted public economic-development investment with substantial executive discretion; the progressive label reflects active public investment, not environmental policy or the wisdom of spending capital receipts.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require state economic-development commitments to companies to be formalized in mutually acceptable written contracts within five years, and void older uncontracted commitments after a transition period.
position_summary: Co-sponsored written-contract and expiration requirements for state economic-development incentive commitments.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The measure increases formal accountability and prevents indefinite informal commitments of public development funds; it does not determine whether incentives themselves should be larger or smaller.

policy_direction_of_yea: Provide small businesses with a nonrefundable $1,000 income or financial-institution excise-tax credit for each qualifying net new Alabama job paying more than $10 per hour after twelve months of continuous employment.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a performance-conditioned small-business tax credit for net job creation above a wage floor.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The bill combines conservative tax reduction with targeted industrial policy and a wage/job-retention condition. Code as mixed rather than forcing the free-market-versus-subsidy divide onto a simple left-right scale.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow retired certified law-enforcement officers in good standing to work part time as Etowah County school resource officers with full police powers, flexible pay, no added benefits, hiring preferences, and civil immunity.
position_summary: Sponsored expanding the pool of armed school law-enforcement personnel through part-time retired officers in Etowah County.
review_note: Full enrolled local act reviewed. The policy expands police presence and authority in schools while reducing employment costs; this is conservative on school security/criminal justice, though it is geographically narrow.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow retired law-enforcement officers in good standing to serve part time as Etowah County school resource officers, waiving physical recertification requirements while retaining certification and full police powers.
position_summary: Sponsored an Etowah County pathway for retired officers to return as part-time school resource officers.
review_note: Full introduced local text reviewed. This predecessor to HB600 likewise expands law-enforcement presence in schools and is coded conservative on school security.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a statewide pathway for retired law-enforcement officers to serve as part-time reserve school resource officers with firearms and use-of-force training but waivers from physical and most continuing-education requirements.
position_summary: Sponsored statewide use of part-time retired officers as armed school resource officers.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The measure expands police staffing and powers in schools using a lower-cost reserve model; certification safeguards temper but do not reverse its conservative school-security direction.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require state-managed hunting lands generally to remain open, replace acreage closed to hunting where required or feasible, coordinate other public lands for replacement access, and report annual gains and losses.
position_summary: Sponsored a statutory no-net-loss policy protecting hunting access on state-owned and state-managed land.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. This is direct evidence of prioritizing rural hunting interests and public hunting access, subject to safety, wildlife-management, security, and park exceptions.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Congress to restore and fully fund the USDA Resource Conservation and Development Program in 2011 and future years because of its natural-resource and rural and urban development work.
position_summary: Co-sponsored continued federal funding for locally led resource-conservation and community-development councils.
review_note: Full House resolution reviewed. Despite being nonbinding, it contains an explicit appropriations position supporting a federal conservation program and is not merely ceremonial.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Congress to restore and fully fund the USDA Resource Conservation and Development Program in 2011 and future years because of its natural-resource and rural and urban development work.
position_summary: Co-sponsored continued federal funding for locally led resource-conservation and community-development councils.
review_note: Full joint resolution reviewed. This companion to HR309 states the same direct conservation-funding position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Raise from $50,000 to $75,000 the salary threshold below which public employees need not file economic-interest statements, and allow employees below that threshold to receive things of value otherwise barred by the ethics law.
position_summary: Sponsored loosening financial-disclosure and gift restrictions for public employees earning less than $75,000.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The policy reduces ethics-law coverage and transparency for a larger group of employees. It may also reduce compliance burdens on non-senior workers, but the operative direction is deregulatory/conservative on government ethics.

policy_direction_of_yea: Cap at $250,000 per election cycle the amount a candidate for statewide office may lend to the candidate's own campaign.
position_summary: Sponsored a limit on candidate self-financing through personal loans in statewide races.
review_note: Full official 2010 First Special Session text reviewed using the repaired ALISON /2010FS/ source. The cap is a campaign-finance restriction intended to constrain personal-wealth advantages and is progressive on election regulation.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require the Secretary of State to maintain a publicly searchable online database of campaign-contribution and expenditure filings by candidate name.
position_summary: Co-sponsored searchable online disclosure of campaign money.
review_note: Full official 2010 First Special Session text reviewed using the repaired ALISON /2010FS/ source. This is direct transparency and campaign-finance reform evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Submit to voters a state-run education lottery funding school resource officers and scholarships without supplanting existing education revenue, while continuing to prohibit casinos.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an education lottery paired with a continued casino ban.
review_note: Full proposed constitutional amendment reviewed. The bill is unambiguously pro-lottery and anti-casino, so a single ideological label would obscure its selective expansion of gambling; retain the concrete stance as mixed.

policy_direction_of_yea: Submit to voters a state-run education lottery funding classroom supplies, school resource officers, and scholarships without supplanting existing education revenue, while continuing to prohibit casinos.
position_summary: Sponsored an education lottery paired with a continued casino ban.
review_note: Full proposed constitutional amendment reviewed. This earlier version states the same selective gambling position as HB308, with an additional classroom-supplies allocation.

policy_direction_of_yea: Broadly expand and standardize firearm-carrying and storage rights, constrain local regulation and permit administration, protect firearms in employees' vehicles, authorize remedies for violations, and repeal the public-demonstration carry ban.
position_summary: Sponsored a comprehensive expansion of state gun-carrying, permit, preemption, reciprocity, and workplace vehicle-storage rights.
review_note: Full bill synopsis and operative structure reviewed. This is strongly directional gun-rights legislation, notwithstanding background-check, eligibility, and location-specific safeguards.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit most employers and property holders from banning lawful firearms or ammunition stored in private vehicles, create civil remedies and employee reinstatement rights, and grant limited liability protection.
position_summary: Sponsored overriding many employer and property rules against lawful firearm storage in private vehicles.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The policy affirmatively expands gun-storage rights at the expense of employer and property-owner discretion and is strong conservative gun-rights evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit most employers and property holders from banning lawful firearms or ammunition stored in private vehicles, create civil remedies and employee reinstatement rights, and grant limited liability protection.
position_summary: Sponsored overriding many employer and property rules against lawful firearm storage in private vehicles.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This 2012 predecessor is materially the same parking-lot gun-rights proposal later introduced as HB12.

policy_direction_of_yea: Increase from 50 percent to 100 percent the additional state income-tax deduction available to qualifying small employers and qualifying employees for employer-plan health-insurance premiums.
position_summary: Co-sponsored doubling a targeted tax deduction designed to make small-business health coverage more affordable.
review_note: Full introduced text and synopsis reviewed. The policy combines a conservative tax-incentive delivery mechanism with a progressive health-coverage objective and income/employer-size targeting; code as mixed.

policy_direction_of_yea: Continue routing Etowah County's receipts from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to the sheriff's law-enforcement fund and retroactively validate those transfers and expenditures.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a local accounting measure continuing ICE-related county receipts in the sheriff's fund.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The act governs the destination of already received money but does not define immigration enforcement, detention policy, or uses beyond the preexisting sheriff fund. Do not infer a broader immigration stance.

policy_direction_of_yea: Subject nearly all property acquired while a person is unlawfully present to civil forfeiture, leave basic necessities to local law-enforcement discretion, and immunize good-faith government action.
position_summary: Co-sponsored sweeping property forfeiture based on unlawful immigration status.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is exceptionally punitive immigration-enforcement evidence: forfeiture is status-based, reaches directly and indirectly acquired property, and contains only a discretionary necessities exception.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow counties, after publishing a fixed project list and winning a local referendum, to levy up to a five-cent-per-gallon motor-fuel tax for road and bridge projects for no more than five years without renewal approval.
position_summary: Co-sponsored local voter authority for a temporary, project-specific gasoline tax dedicated to roads and bridges.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The measure authorizes a tax increase and public infrastructure investment but requires direct voter approval, project transparency, a rate cap, and sunset; code as mixed.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require multi-year salary increases for public-education employees and cost-of-living adjustments for Teachers' Retirement System retirees, including at least five percent in fiscal 2014 followed by 2.5 percent increases.
position_summary: Sponsored substantial multi-year raises for public-school employees and pension cost-of-living adjustments for education retirees.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is direct, strongly directional support for educator compensation and retirement benefits, with required future appropriations.

policy_direction_of_yea: Restore the state's commitment to full PACT prepaid-tuition benefits, tie payments to current tuition and mandatory fees, extend tuition-growth limits across Alabama institutions, constrain investment risk, and permit the program to reopen.
position_summary: Sponsored restoring promised prepaid-college benefits while limiting tuition growth and investment risk.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The bill favors beneficiaries and affordable higher education through an enforceable state commitment, though it also adds prudential financial controls.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a new optional Deferred Retirement Option Plan allowing eligible long-service teachers and state employees below an income ceiling to keep working while retirement benefits accrue in a time-limited account.
position_summary: Sponsored restoring a structured deferred-retirement benefit for eligible teachers and state employees.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The measure expands benefit flexibility for long-serving public workers, subject to age, service, income, duration, contribution, and forfeiture safeguards.

policy_direction_of_yea: Mourn the death of Belle Farmer and extend sympathy to her family and friends.
position_summary: Sponsored a constituent memorial resolution.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. This is ceremonial and provides no social-services or ideological evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Recognize the Alabama Student Angler Bass Fishing Association.
position_summary: Sponsored a ceremonial recognition of a student fishing organization.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. The recognition reflects local sporting interest but creates no hunting, fishing, education, or conservation policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Use up to $15 million in Education Trust Fund revenue left unobligated because Alabama Accountability Act tax-credit costs were below forecast for the Alabama Math, Science, and Technology Initiative.
position_summary: Co-sponsored redirecting unused school-choice tax-credit reserves to a public-school math, science, and technology program.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. Contrary to the compact title's possible ambiguity, the appropriation does not finance Accountability Act credits; it uses the lower-than-expected credit cost to supplement AMSTI.

policy_direction_of_yea: Transfer PACT assets and future appropriations among higher-education institutions and require Alabama public colleges to honor the full tuition-and-fee terms promised in remaining prepaid-tuition contracts.
position_summary: Co-sponsored requiring state colleges and PACT resources to fulfill prepaid-college tuition promises despite a projected funding shortfall.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The proposal protects contract beneficiaries and directs public institutions and future appropriations toward full promised benefits.

policy_direction_of_yea: Transfer PACT assets and future appropriations among higher-education institutions and require Alabama public colleges to honor the full tuition-and-fee terms promised in remaining prepaid-tuition contracts.
position_summary: Sponsored requiring state colleges and PACT resources to fulfill prepaid-college tuition promises despite a projected funding shortfall.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This 2013 predecessor states materially the same beneficiary-protection policy as the 2014 HB309.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit adult sex offenders from residing within 2,000 feet of a public park or playground and impose criminal penalties for violations.
position_summary: Co-sponsored expanding residency exclusions and penalties for people convicted of sex offenses.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is direct punitive criminal-justice evidence, notwithstanding its child-safety rationale and the broader existing residency regime.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require nearly all Alabama businesses and public employers to verify new employees' work authorization through E-Verify or another reasonable method and suspend business licenses for violations.
position_summary: Co-sponsored mandatory employment-authorization verification backed by business-license penalties.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is direct state-level immigration-enforcement evidence imposing broad employer duties and sanctions.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create performance-linked state payments and authorize school-construction bonds for Huntsville and North Alabama infrastructure needed to accommodate Redstone Arsenal growth from the 2005 BRAC process.
position_summary: Co-sponsored public infrastructure and school investment tied to military-base job growth in North Alabama.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The bill uses public payments and bonding to support regional economic expansion and school capacity, making it active public-investment evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require school boards to notify teachers by the end of the school term if loss of a supplemental position will reduce their compensation for the next year.
position_summary: Co-sponsored advance written notice protecting teachers from unexpected loss of supplemental pay.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The bill creates a modest procedural employment protection without guaranteeing continued supplemental assignments or pay.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend Tuskegee University's basketball team for winning its conference championship.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of Tuskegee University's basketball team.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. This companion commendation is non-substantive and provides no higher-education position evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow Limestone County's existing sales-and-use-tax receipts to pay refinanced debt for the same authorized public buildings and terminate the tax after all original or refunding debt is paid.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a local debt-refinancing clarification for an existing earmarked sales tax.
review_note: Full introduced local text reviewed. This changes debt administration but neither authorizes a new tax nor reveals a general tax or spending position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require the Alabama Network of Family Resource Centers to adopt allocation rules for state and federal funds and publish advance notice of proposed rules in the Alabama Administrative Monthly.
position_summary: Co-sponsored transparent rulemaking for distribution of public funding among family resource centers.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The bill is procedural rather than a new appropriation, but it directly supports transparency and standardized allocation in a social-services network.

policy_direction_of_yea: Grandfather economic-development projects whose companies filed intent statements by November 21, 2009, under the earlier base-wage requirement rather than a newer wage threshold.
position_summary: Co-sponsored delaying a higher base-wage requirement for already developing tax-incentive projects.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The transition rule favors project continuity and lower employer wage requirements over immediate application of the newer labor standard; it is conservative on wage conditions, though limited to a grandfathered cohort.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow qualifying first-time felony offenders serving life without parole for capital murder to obtain life with parole eligibility after twenty years and sustained records free of serious prison misconduct, with retroactive review.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a narrowly conditioned, retroactive second-chance pathway for some capital offenders serving life without parole.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is strong sentencing-reform evidence while retaining a twenty-year minimum and extensive conduct safeguards.

policy_direction_of_yea: Restore TANF and food-assistance eligibility to otherwise qualified people with drug-felony convictions after sentence completion or during satisfactory probation and required treatment.
position_summary: Co-sponsored ending Alabama's lifetime food-aid and cash-assistance exclusion for many people with drug felony records.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The policy supports reintegration and access to the safety net, conditioned on sentence, probation, and treatment compliance.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create state licensure, form approval, disclosures, examinations, reporting, and civil and criminal enforcement for life-settlement providers and brokers under the Insurance Commissioner.
position_summary: Co-sponsored comprehensive consumer-protection regulation of the life-settlement industry.
review_note: Full introduced structure and synopsis reviewed. The act adds substantial market regulation and disclosure duties intended to protect policyholders, making it progressive on occupational and financial-services regulation.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow former legislative, judicial, and executive employees age 50 or older with at least 24 months of service and 18 months of coverage to remain in the state employee health plan at their own full cost.
position_summary: Co-sponsored continued group-health-plan access for qualifying former state employees without a state premium subsidy.
review_note: Full engrossed text reviewed. The measure expands benefit access but expressly places the entire cost on the former employee, making it a modest rather than expansive public benefit.

policy_direction_of_yea: End future supernumerary status for the Cullman County sheriff and revenue commissioner and allow participation in the regular Employees' Retirement System, while grandfathering existing rights and permitting service-credit purchase.
position_summary: Co-sponsored replacing two county officials' supernumerary system with ordinary state employee retirement participation.
review_note: Full proposed local constitutional amendment reviewed. This modernizes and regularizes retirement treatment but preserves accrued rights and permits credit purchase; code as mixed institutional benefit reform.

policy_direction_of_yea: Transfer the State Board of Education's fiscal-year 2011 share of Children First Trust Fund receipts to the State General Fund.
position_summary: Co-sponsored diverting an earmarked education allocation from the Children First Trust Fund into the General Fund for one fiscal year.
review_note: Full enrolled text reviewed. The bill reduces the statutory protection of a public-education funding stream, though the ultimate General Fund use is unspecified; classify the observable diversion, not an assumed spending cut.

policy_direction_of_yea: Give the Attorney General exclusive direction and control over state civil and criminal litigation and investigations, bar the governor from initiating or directing them, and void prior contrary actions.
position_summary: Co-sponsored shifting state litigation and investigative authority from the governor to the independently elected attorney general.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is a clear separation-of-powers position but not inherently left or right; code as mixed institutional governance.

policy_direction_of_yea: Broaden and modernize Alabama's civil Protection From Abuse Act to cover dating relationships and threats, expand remedies and enforcement, create a statewide registry, and coordinate custody and interstate-order procedures.
position_summary: Co-sponsored broader and more accessible civil protection-order safeguards for domestic-violence victims.
review_note: Full introduced purpose and operative structure reviewed. Repeal of duplicative criminal provisions does not reverse the bill's expressly victim-protective civil expansion.

policy_direction_of_yea: Abolish the common-law rule barring homicide prosecution when the victim dies more than a year and a day after the causal act.
position_summary: Co-sponsored expanding homicide liability to deaths occurring beyond the former year-and-a-day limit.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The act removes a defense and broadens prosecutorial reach, making it modestly conservative/punitive on criminal justice.

policy_direction_of_yea: Define a child for chemical-endangerment prosecution to include an unborn child at any stage regardless of viability and create a rebuttable presumption from matching positive drug tests at birth.
position_summary: Co-sponsored criminal prosecution of prenatal drug exposure using fetal-personhood language and an evidentiary presumption against the mother.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is strongly punitive criminal-justice evidence with an additional anti-abortion/fetal-personhood valence; code primarily under criminal justice to avoid treating drug exposure as a general abortion position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend a regional Resource Conservation and Development Council for an award and for community and conservation projects.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of a regional conservation council.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. Although it lists substantive conservation accomplishments, the act only honors an award recipient and is not reliable individual policy evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require affected county and municipal approval, findings, public notice, hearings, and information access before ADEM may issue or modify granite or limestone surface-mining permits.
position_summary: Co-sponsored local veto authority and public environmental review for surface-mining permits.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. The proposal adds substantial environmental, health, infrastructure, property-value, and public-participation safeguards before mining approval.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit political action committees from transferring contributions to other PACs, except principal campaign committees.
position_summary: Sponsored a ban on PAC-to-PAC transfers intended to improve campaign-money traceability.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is direct campaign-finance transparency and anti-circumvention evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Limit each political action committee's contributions to a candidate to $1,000 per election cycle.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a $1,000 cap on PAC contributions to individual candidates.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is direct campaign-finance restriction evidence aimed at limiting organized-money influence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Recognize the University of West Alabama's 175th anniversary.
position_summary: Joined a chamber-wide ceremonial recognition of the University of West Alabama.
review_note: Full resolution reviewed. The historical commendation creates no higher-education policy or funding commitment.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow permitted sales of farm-raised yellow perch under the same exception already available for specified hatchery and farm-pond fish.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a narrow deregulation benefiting farm-pond aquaculture while retaining permits and wild game-fish sale restrictions.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. This is modest rural-business and aquaculture deregulation, not a change to wild-fish conservation rules.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create and fund a third elected circuit judgeship for Marshall County beginning with the 2012 general election after Voting Rights Act preclearance.
position_summary: Sponsored additional local judicial capacity in the Twenty-seventh Judicial Circuit.
review_note: Full introduced text reviewed. Adding a judge is a concrete local service priority but supplies no dependable ideological or issue-direction evidence for the state matrix.

policy_direction_of_yea: Redistribute TVA in-lieu-of-tax payments among TVA-served jurisdictions and dry non-TVA communities while offsetting parts of the latter allocation with liquor-tax receipts.
position_summary: Co-sponsored revising the geographic distribution of TVA and alcohol-related local revenues.
review_note: Full enrolled structure reviewed. The bill is distributive local fiscal policy with winners and offsets rather than a general tax increase or cut; retain as mixed.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a multidisciplinary statewide team to standardize and coordinate investigation of sudden unexplained infant deaths.
position_summary: Co-sponsored coordinated state investigation and prevention capacity for sudden unexplained infant deaths.
review_note: Official bill synopsis reviewed. The measure expands public-health and child-welfare coordination rather than criminalizing parents or changing benefits.

policy_direction_of_yea: Further restrict over-the-counter ephedrine and pseudoephedrine sales through real-time electronic verification, penalties, and a Drug Abuse Task Force.
position_summary: Co-sponsored expanded controlled-substance precursor monitoring and enforcement.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The bill's dominant direction is stricter drug enforcement, although it also has a public-health rationale.

policy_direction_of_yea: Recognize the Concerns of Police Survivors Fly the Blue Campaign.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial recognition of a police-survivor organization and campaign.
review_note: Official resolution synopsis reviewed. This is symbolic support for law-enforcement families, not a criminal-justice policy position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend Jesse Owens and name a segment of Highway 36 the Jesse Owens Parkway.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an honorary highway designation for Jesse Owens.
review_note: Official resolution synopsis reviewed. The action is commemorative and non-policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Appropriate Education Trust Fund money to Talladega College subject to state fiscal controls.
position_summary: Co-sponsored state higher-education funding for Talladega College.
review_note: Official appropriation text and synopsis reviewed. This is direct support for public investment in a historically Black private college serving an educational public purpose.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow Shoals Economic Development Fund money to support workforce training and economic-development programs at the University of North Alabama.
position_summary: Co-sponsored using regional development funds for university-based workforce training and economic development.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The measure expands permissible public investment in workforce capacity.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow Shoals Economic Development Fund money to construct a Workforce Training and Development Center.
position_summary: Co-sponsored regional public investment in a workforce training center.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct workforce-development infrastructure evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Urge Congress to review commercial-driver-license mandates and remove unnecessary burdens on agriculture and small businesses.
position_summary: Co-sponsored federal regulatory relief for agricultural and small-business vehicle operators.
review_note: Official resolution synopsis reviewed. This is explicit deregulatory advocacy centered on rural and small-business interests.

policy_direction_of_yea: Criminalize interference with, injury to, or intentional killing of a service animal and require restitution.
position_summary: Co-sponsored stronger legal protection for service-animal users and restitution for harm.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The disability-access protection is progressive even though enforcement uses criminal penalties.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize local public-school security forces and define their relationship with local law enforcement.
position_summary: Sponsored establishment of dedicated security forces in public K-12 schools.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The policy expands institutional security and policing capacity in schools.

policy_direction_of_yea: Permit a seat-belt citation when a person is stopped and arrested for a separate violation.
position_summary: Sponsored limited secondary enforcement of Alabama's seat-belt requirement.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The measure expands safety-law enforcement only after an independent stop and arrest, making the regulatory direction progressive but narrow.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a hunting license for disabled residents that remains valid while the disability continues.
position_summary: Sponsored more accessible, durable hunting licensure for people with disabilities.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is a rural sporting-access measure with a disability-accommodation direction.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit state agencies from adopting fuel-economy regulation or a cap-and-trade program without legislative authorization.
position_summary: Co-sponsored blocking administrative climate and fuel-economy regulation absent a separate legislative act.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is explicit conservative environmental and regulatory policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Exclude third-party rewards for exemplary public service from the ethics-law ban on using office for personal gain.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a new ethics-law exception allowing certain third-party rewards to public officials.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Whatever its employee-recognition rationale, the operative direction loosens ethics restrictions and creates a gift-like exception.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit political action committees from transferring money to other PACs except principal campaign committees.
position_summary: Sponsored a PAC-to-PAC transfer ban to improve campaign-finance traceability.
review_note: Full repaired 2010 First Special Session text was previously validated and reviewed. This is direct campaign-finance reform evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize qualified local-board school security personnel and resource officers to carry firearms under specified conditions.
position_summary: Co-sponsored arming qualified school security personnel and resource officers.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct conservative gun and school-security evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create crimes for knowingly soliciting an unlawful firearm transfer or deliberately giving false information to a gun seller, with stated exceptions and penalties.
position_summary: Sponsored additional criminal enforcement against unlawful and deceptive firearm purchases.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The measure strengthens gun-sale enforcement while targeting already unlawful or knowingly deceptive conduct rather than lawful possession.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require law-enforcement agencies to dispose of seized firearms through auctions to eligible purchasers and retain proceeds for law-enforcement purposes.
position_summary: Sponsored returning seized firearms to lawful commerce through auction instead of destruction.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The policy favors lawful gun circulation and law-enforcement revenue and is conservative on firearms.

policy_direction_of_yea: Recognize Red Bay Hospital for fifty years of service.
position_summary: Sponsored a ceremonial hospital anniversary recognition.
review_note: Official resolution synopsis reviewed. No health financing or delivery policy is enacted.

policy_direction_of_yea: Recognize Red Bay Hospital for fifty years of service.
position_summary: Sponsored a ceremonial hospital anniversary recognition.
review_note: Official joint-resolution synopsis reviewed. This companion is non-policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize blood and saliva testing and specified disclosure after offenders expose law-enforcement officers, firefighters, first responders, or corrections officers to communicable disease in the line of duty.
position_summary: Co-sponsored occupational disease-testing protections for first responders that compel testing and limited health-information disclosure from offenders.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Worker safety is protective while involuntary testing and offender privacy burdens are coercive; code as mixed.

policy_direction_of_yea: Name a segment of U.S. Highway 72 for Frankie Lee Wallace.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an honorary highway designation.
review_note: Official resolution synopsis reviewed. This is ceremonial, not infrastructure policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Expand the Franklin County Water Coordinating and Fire Prevention Authority's permissible services to include sewage and broadband.
position_summary: Sponsored expansion of a public local authority into sewer and broadband service.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is active public-service and infrastructure expansion.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize a Franklin County sales tax for schools, temporarily allocate a portion to roads, and require a referendum for extension.
position_summary: Sponsored a locally approved sales tax supporting schools and roads with a time-limited allocation and renewal vote.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The bill combines a regressive revenue instrument with public education and infrastructure investment plus voter control.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow the Retirement Systems of Alabama secretary-treasurer to make investment decisions without Board of Control approval.
position_summary: Sponsored concentrating RSA investment authority in its secretary-treasurer.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is a clear governance-centralization position but has no stable left-right direction absent evidence about safeguards and performance.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend the University of North Alabama on its 180th anniversary.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial university anniversary resolution.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. No education policy or appropriation is created.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend the George Lindsey University of North Alabama Film Festival.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial film-festival commendation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is cultural recognition, not education policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Award correctional officers one year of hazardous-duty service credit for every five years worked for retirement and insurance purposes.
position_summary: Sponsored enhanced retirement recognition for correctional officers' hazardous service.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This expands public-worker benefits for a high-risk occupation.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a Lauderdale County Community Development Fund and divide expenditures between the county commission and a development authority after formation of an agriculture authority.
position_summary: Sponsored a local structure for distributing community-development resources between public bodies.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The measure establishes a development priority but the compact description does not expose enough allocation detail for a directional ideological code.

policy_direction_of_yea: Use Lauderdale County TVA in-lieu-of-tax community-development money to provide sheriff's officers uniforms and a uniform allowance, retroactive to 2006.
position_summary: Sponsored public funding of work uniforms and allowances for county sheriff's officers.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is a narrow employee-compensation and equipment benefit.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create optional personalized memorial license plates for deceased family members, charge an additional fee, and send proceeds to the General Fund.
position_summary: Sponsored a fee-supported memorial license-plate option.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This consumer option and fee is administrative and not useful ideological evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Constitutionally prohibit abortion except to preserve the pregnant woman's life or when pregnancy results from rape or incest, with penalties.
position_summary: Sponsored a constitutional abortion ban with life, rape, and incest exceptions.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct anti-abortion policy evidence, with broader exceptions than Alabama's later near-total statutory ban.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit private or denominational hospitals from requiring employees or physicians to participate in abortion, embryo research, cloning, euthanasia, or assisted suicide and create civil remedies.
position_summary: Sponsored broad institutional and worker conscience protections against participation in specified reproductive and end-of-life procedures.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct conservative health-care conscience evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend the Pike County Economic Development Corporation.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of a local development corporation.
review_note: Official resolution synopsis reviewed. Recognition alone does not establish a subsidy or development-policy stance.

policy_direction_of_yea: Provide salary increases for specified Department of Corrections employees working inside secured facilities.
position_summary: Sponsored increased compensation for corrections employees working inside security fences.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct support for higher pay for hazardous public work and parallels HB747.

policy_direction_of_yea: Classify assault on an off-duty law-enforcement officer performing lawful private security work as second-degree assault under the officer-protection statute.
position_summary: Sponsored extending enhanced assault penalties to off-duty officers employed by private entities.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The measure broadens a penalty enhancement and is punitive/conservative on criminal justice.

policy_direction_of_yea: Establish crimes and penalties for coercive or deceptive labor and sex trafficking.
position_summary: Sponsored explicit criminal prohibitions against human trafficking and exploitation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Protection from exploitation is progressive while the delivery mechanism is punitive criminal enforcement; the issue is substantively important but not cleanly partisan.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a continuously valid hunting and fishing license for qualifying disabled veterans.
position_summary: Sponsored durable, lower-burden hunting and fishing access for disabled veterans.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This combines rural sporting access with a disability and veterans accommodation.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require the Ethics Commission to provide mandatory ethics training for elected officials.
position_summary: Sponsored mandatory ethics-law training for elected officials.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct good-government and compliance evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create a voluntarily funded annuity and benefit system for paid and volunteer firefighters with service, disability, and death benefits, professional administration, audits, and reports.
position_summary: Sponsored a new voluntary retirement and survivor-benefit program for firefighters.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This expands structured benefits for public-safety workers while relying on voluntary participation and dedicated funding.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create an Alzheimer's Disease Task Force to assess statewide present and future needs and report recommendations.
position_summary: Sponsored state planning for Alzheimer's disease services and policy.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The task force is a substantive health and aging priority even though it does not itself appropriate services.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize hospitals and long-term-care providers to donate unused prescription drugs and physician samples to charitable pharmacies and clinics under regulated conditions.
position_summary: Sponsored a prescription-drug donation pathway for charitable health providers.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The policy expands access to medicines through regulated reuse and charitable distribution.

policy_direction_of_yea: Dedicate $100 million annually from the Alabama Trust Fund for ten years to state and local road, bridge, rail, maintenance, and economic-development infrastructure.
position_summary: Sponsored a decade-long state and local transportation investment program funded from Trust Fund assets.
review_note: Official synopsis and House-companion text reviewed. This is active public infrastructure investment with a real Trust Fund tradeoff.

policy_direction_of_yea: Name a segment of Alabama Highway 113 for Dewey J. Bondurant Jr.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an honorary highway designation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. No transportation policy is created.

policy_direction_of_yea: Name a segment of Interstate 65 for Ray Scott.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an honorary highway designation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. No transportation policy is created.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow designated Etowah County sales-tax revenue to support salaries of certified school personnel and Gadsden State employees during proration.
position_summary: Sponsored protecting education employee salaries with earmarked local revenue during budget proration.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct educator-compensation protection, though geographically and fiscally conditional.

policy_direction_of_yea: Alter the constitutional age requirement for members of the University of Alabama Board of Trustees.
position_summary: Sponsored a governance eligibility change for university trustees.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Without a substantive policy consequence in the compact record, an age-rule adjustment is not reliable ideological evidence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend the White House HBCU Initiative and Alabama A&M University for hosting a technical-assistance conference.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial HBCU conference commendation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Recognition does not enact education policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Exempt the National Voting Rights Museum and Institute from state income and state and local sales and use taxes.
position_summary: Sponsored tax support for an institution preserving voting-rights and civil-rights history.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is narrow but direct material support for a civil-rights institution.

policy_direction_of_yea: Centralize livestock and animal-husbandry regulation in the Agriculture Department and State Veterinarian while revising animal-cruelty enforcement.
position_summary: Sponsored state preemption and consolidation of livestock regulation with animal-health and cruelty provisions.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Agricultural regulatory uniformity is conservative, while disease and cruelty enforcement can be protective; code as mixed rural/agriculture policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Add an Etowah County solicitor fee and court costs and direct the proceeds under a companion constitutional amendment.
position_summary: Sponsored additional criminal and court fees in Etowah County.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This expands fee-based justice-system financing and is conservative/punitive in effect.

policy_direction_of_yea: Charge an application fee for interstate adult-offender supervision transfers, permit exemptions, and continuously appropriate proceeds to probation upkeep.
position_summary: Sponsored user-fee financing for interstate probation and parole transfer administration.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The measure places added financial burden on supervised people, subject to exceptions.

policy_direction_of_yea: Apply salary reductions consistently to state-employed and specified county-employed juvenile probation officers.
position_summary: Sponsored consistent pay reductions across juvenile-probation employment arrangements.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The compact text indicates a benefit cut but does not expose its size or fiscal context, so confidence is medium.

policy_direction_of_yea: Substantially strengthen Alabama ethics law through broader definitions, disclosure, subpoena authority, lobbying and contracting restrictions, and increased bribery, conflict, and trading-in-office penalties.
position_summary: Sponsored a comprehensive expansion of ethics disclosure, enforcement, and anti-corruption restrictions.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is strong good-government reform evidence despite its use of enhanced penalties.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create and constitutionally authorize a Gaming Commission to regulate and tax commercial bingo and distribute proceeds.
position_summary: Sponsored legalized, regulated, and taxed commercial bingo.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The concrete stance is pro-regulated gambling; because Alabama gambling coalitions cross conventional ideology, retain a mixed valence.

policy_direction_of_yea: Increase the Choctaw County concealed-pistol permit fee.
position_summary: Sponsored a local increase in the cost of concealed-pistol permits.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is modestly progressive on gun regulation but narrow and revenue-oriented.

policy_direction_of_yea: Prohibit text messaging while driving on public roads and impose penalties.
position_summary: Sponsored a statewide distracted-driving safety prohibition.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The measure expands safety regulation and enforcement rather than general criminal punishment.

policy_direction_of_yea: Commend teachers and educational support personnel.
position_summary: Co-sponsored a ceremonial commendation of education workers.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Recognition alone is not evidence of pay, funding, or labor policy.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require revocation of education certification or termination of school employment after conviction of a felony or a child-related sex offense.
position_summary: Sponsored mandatory professional exclusion of education workers convicted of specified crimes.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The policy removes discretion and imposes a collateral employment consequence, making it punitive/conservative.

policy_direction_of_yea: Require revocation of education certification or termination of school employment after conviction of a felony or a child-related sex offense.
position_summary: Sponsored mandatory professional exclusion of education workers convicted of specified crimes.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This companion states the same punitive employment consequence as SB316.

policy_direction_of_yea: Extend the Lieutenant Governor's Commission on Public-Private Partnership Projects.
position_summary: Sponsored continuing state study and implementation work on public-private infrastructure partnerships.
review_note: Official synopsis and House-companion text reviewed. The extension establishes a P3 priority but incorporates recommendations not restated here, so no simple ideological direction is assigned.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize Forestry Commission administrative rules governing conduct on state forests and penalties for violations.
position_summary: Sponsored enforceable conduct rules on state forest land.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. Resource stewardship and rule enforcement are substantive, but the compact description does not show whether particular restrictions expand conservation, recreation access, or agency power enough for a directional code.

policy_direction_of_yea: Redirect part of Citronelle oil-and-gas revenue to a volunteer fire department in place of a rescue squad and release specified escrowed funds.
position_summary: Sponsored local energy-revenue support for volunteer fire protection.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is public-safety service funding through local resource revenue, though it reallocates rather than creates money.

policy_direction_of_yea: Create an additional Baldwin County circuit judgeship with conditional state appropriations.
position_summary: Sponsored additional local judicial capacity.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The service-capacity choice has no dependable ideological direction in the available text.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize an income-tax deduction for employers hiring qualifying unemployment-benefit recipients or people whose benefits expired.
position_summary: Sponsored a targeted tax incentive for reemployment of unemployed workers.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The bill combines a conservative tax mechanism with a progressive labor-market objective and is coded mixed.

policy_direction_of_yea: Revise film-production tax rebates and limit related sales, use, and lodging exemptions to the state-tax portion.
position_summary: Sponsored targeted entertainment-industry incentives while narrowing which tax shares are exempt.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is industrial policy with both subsidy expansion/adjustment and a local-revenue limitation.

policy_direction_of_yea: Add a Cleburne County drug-and-violent-crime court fee and distribute proceeds to the circuit clerk, sheriff, and regional task force.
position_summary: Sponsored fee-financed drug and violent-crime enforcement.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This expands court-cost burdens and funds punitive enforcement.

policy_direction_of_yea: Authorize additional Cleburne County court costs in traffic, civil, and criminal cases and distribute the revenue locally.
position_summary: Co-sponsored broader local court-cost financing.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. The policy increases user fees across justice proceedings and is conservative on fee-based court finance.

policy_direction_of_yea: Allow Cherokee County sheriff's deputies retiring with at least ten years of service to receive a badge, commission card, and pistol without cost.
position_summary: Sponsored a free service pistol and credentials benefit for qualifying retired deputies.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is both a public-employee recognition benefit and a narrow gun-rights position.

policy_direction_of_yea: Credit qualifying military service and other covered public employment when calculating the retiree sliding-scale premium in the State Employees' Health Insurance Plan.
position_summary: Co-sponsored broader service credit to reduce or improve retiree health-premium treatment.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. This is direct benefit protection for public servants and veterans.

policy_direction_of_yea: Designate a Cleburne County highway segment as the Lieutenant Ralph Byron Bentley Memorial Highway.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an honorary memorial highway designation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. No infrastructure policy is created.

policy_direction_of_yea: Name a Cherokee County highway segment for W. A. Ellis Jr.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an honorary highway designation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. No infrastructure policy is created.

policy_direction_of_yea: Name a Cherokee County U.S. Highway 411 segment for George and Tom Jordan.
position_summary: Co-sponsored an honorary highway designation.
review_note: Official synopsis reviewed. No infrastructure policy is created.
